$comment: Per-environment Salesforce endpoint and the distribution lists that drive each pipeline.
The destination mailbox is the ONLY thing that selects the operation — the CSV bytes for
an initial load and a shipment update are identical. So a wrong address is a silent no-op
or a double load, and every send is matched on the mailbox's LOCAL PART before it goes.
Resolution order for a (family, operation) pair:
1. byFamilyOperation['<family>:<operation>']   — a family that has its own mailbox
2. byOperation['<operation>']                  — the shared mailbox for that operation
Any value still carrying the REPLACE_ME sentinel blocks sending for that pipeline, so an
unconfirmed address is safe to leave in place rather than a hazard.
Verified: both Salesforce endpoints, and byOperation.initialLoad and
byOperation.shipmentUpdate for testing. The staging mailboxes and the dataUpdate and
received mailboxes are UNCONFIRMED — see README.
instanceUrl carries no trailing slash: the REST path is appended to it directly, and a
double slash before /services/data is rejected.

$comment: How mail leaves the app.
outlook-web — drive Outlook on the web with Playwright. The default, because SMTP is not
usable in this tenant: it returns 535 5.7.139, which is Microsoft's code for
SMTP AUTH being disabled for the tenant or mailbox. No app password can get
past that; only an admin re-enabling basic auth would, and Microsoft has
deprecated it.
smtp        — kept so it can be switched back if SMTP AUTH is ever re-enabled.
autoSend applies to outlook-web. Left false, the app fills the compose window and stops so
you read it and press Send. Turn it on once you trust what it produces — a wrong send here
is a real device load.

smtp.$comment: Host/port only. Username and password are entered in the UI per session. Currently unusable — see mail.$comment.

sentItemsCheck.$comment: IMAP is used only to confirm the message reached Sent Items.
